---
title: "Deploy on Dokploy"
description: "Deploy Openinary on Dokploy by importing a ready-made Compose configuration."
---

Dokploy runs Openinary as a Compose service. The base64 blob below carries the image, the port, the volumes and the variables, so you paste one config instead of filling forms. You need a Dokploy account with access to a server, and Docker support enabled on that instance.

## Deployment steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Create a Compose service">

In your project, create a new service. Choose **Compose** as the service type, set the name to **Openinary**, select **Docker Compose** as the compose type, and click **Create**.

No project yet? Create one first, then open its dashboard.

</Step>

<Step title="Import the configuration">

Go to the **Advanced** tab, scroll to the **Import** section, and paste this base64 config:

```bash

```

Click **Load**, then **Import**. The configuration is imported automatically once it validates.

</Step>

<Step title="Check the environment variables">

The import pre-configures the variables with placeholders:

```bash
IMAGE_TAG=latest
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=your-sha256-hash-or-long-secret
BETTER_AUTH_URL=your-dokploy-generated-url-or-domain
```

Set `BETTER_AUTH_URL` to your base URL, the domain where Openinary will be accessible.

The template is pre-configured for local storage, so nothing more is needed there. For an S3-compatible bucket, add its configuration:

```bash
STORAGE_REGION=your-region
STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-access-key
STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret-key
STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME=your-bucket-name
STORAGE_ENDPOINT=https://your-s3-endpoint.com
STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL=https://your-cdn-domain.com
```

See the [Storage configuration](/configuration/storage) page for detailed setup instructions.

</Step>

<Step title="Deploy">

Verify everything in the **Environment** tab, click **Deploy**, then **Confirm**. The deployment logs end with:

```
Docker Compose Deployed: ✅
```

</Step>

<Step title="Create your admin account">

Go to the **Domains** tab and visit the generated URL or your configured custom domain. You land on the initial setup page.

<Warning>
  Create the admin account immediately. The setup route is publicly accessible until it is completed.
</Warning>

After signing in, the dashboard shows the sample assets or your bucket content.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Troubleshooting

Check the deployment logs in Dokploy for error messages, verify every environment variable, and confirm your DNS if you use a custom domain. If problems persist, [create an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/openinary/openinary/issues) with your deployment logs.
